river.name: Cauvery
river.to: Poompuhar, Bay of Bengal, Tamil Nadu (79.8579, 11.1367)

drains.note: NO measured drain exists for the Cauvery in any source used: every drain row is an estimate (untreated flow x 250 mg/l raw-sewage BOD, Ganga v1.1 method) or unmeasured (flow not published). Measured and estimated totals are separate and are never summed into a single "total pollution" figure. The biggest estimated load is the Vrishabhavathi valley outflow from Bengaluru (215 MLD, 53.75 TPD, 2017 vintage) — 80.5% of the estimated BOD total; it is a 2017 estimate, and Bengaluru treatment capacity has since risen to 390 MLD.

top_10_by_bod_tpd.drain: Kollegala unconnected areas (HosaAnagalli, Shankanapura, Upparamole, Bendarahalli, Booditittu)
Mullur Gram Panchayat drains (2 drains, aggregate)

stps.note: Compliance is mapped from the MPRs' single "Complied/Complying" flag: it means the plant meets the consent standard (BOD 20 mg/l, i.e. the MoEFCC 2017 norm), so it meets MoEFCC; NGT compliance (BOD 10 mg/l) cannot be inferred from a consent flag and is left null. NO Cauvery plant in the sources used has a published per-plant effluent BOD value, so 0 plants are shown meeting NGT norms — a DATA LIMIT, not a finding. All 65 operational/under-trial plants carry the Complied flag (Karnataka MPR Nov 2025, TN MPR Aug 2026); the 3 under-construction plants are unassessed. The older Karnataka MPR Jan 2025 flagged Ramanagara and Kanakapura Non-complying; the Nov 2025 annexure supersedes it (see stps_NOTES.md). No operator is named per plant in the TN MPR; Karnataka plants list BWSSB (Bengaluru) or KUWS&DB / concerned ULB.

worst_stretch.stretch: Mettur to Mayiladuthurai (200 km), Tamil Nadu
worst_stretch.priority: II (CPCB Oct 2025 revision; Priority I in 2018)
worst_stretch.basis: CPCB Oct 2025 revision (2022-23 basis), via TN MPR Aug 2026
worst_stretch.worst_station: Erode near Chirapalayam — BOD 17.0 mg/l, DO 1.5 mg/l (CPCB 2009, earliest snapshot)
worst_stretch.karnataka_stretch: Ranganathittu to Satyagala Bridge, BOD 3.1-6.7 mg/l, Priority IV (CPCB 2022 report); 2025-revision status unknown
worst_stretch.note: The worst-station figure (Erode, BOD 17.0) is from 2009 — the most recent per-station value published for the Tamil Nadu reach. The most recent per-station values anywhere are Mar 2023 (KSPCB): Lakshmantirtha D/S Hunsur and D/S Kattemalavadi, BOD 8.0 mg/l each; Arkavathi D/S Kanakapura, BOD 7.0 mg/l.

water_quality.note: Series years are SNAPSHOTS, not a like-for-like series: 2009 = CPCB annual-summary values (Tamil Nadu stations only); 2022 = KSPCB March monthly samples; 2023 = KSPCB March monthly samples; 2025 = Karnataka MPR Jan 2025 single-month samples (4 main-stem stations). The 2009 values sit in bod_earliest/bod_latest only — the schema year columns start at 2014, so no bod_2009 column exists (see wq_NOTES.md). Trends are indicative only. The TN MPR Aug 2026 gives only a range for the Cauvery (BOD 2.0-4.7 mg/l across 19 stations), no per-station values, so there are no 2026 values. No pH values are published for any Cauvery station in the sources used.

people.note: The summed town population is NOT the corridor population; see population below. Tamil Nadu MLAs are the 2026 election winners (polling 23 Apr 2026, results 4 May 2026; hung assembly: TVK 108, DMK 59, AIADMK 47, INC 5). Karnataka MLAs are the 2023 election winners.

industries.note: 8 aggregate rows. Karnataka: Vrishabhavathi Valley industrial belt (191 industries, 8.008 MLD effluent generated) plus Srirangapatna, Bannur, T Narasipura and Kollegala town aggregates (0.0196-0.027 MLD each). Tamil Nadu: Trichy CETP (0.2014 MLD reported), Perundurai CETPs (3.681 MLD reported), Tiruppur CETPs (65.096 MLD reported — most Tiruppur CETPs claim ZLD, so treat as reported, not verified). Effluent figures are consented/reported figures, never measurements, and are not added to any drain load.
